articles.title: Agnes Hobart, 85, Church Organist
articles.deck: Friends remember Agnes Hobart for the many years of service to Upper Commons.
body: Born in Upper Commons in the years after the war, Agnes Hobart spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Agnes Hobart died in May at home on Dover Place, at the age of 85.
Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to St. Brendan’s Parish in his or her name.

articles.title: Council Splits 4–3 on Street Tree Planting
articles.deck: The vote came after 9 residents spoke at Sunday’s session.
body: Councilmember Celia Fairbanks asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $48,000. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Residents of Tannery Flats said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.
Public works estimates the work will take about 9 weeks once it starts in May.

articles.title: Ellis Corrigan Named Coordinator of the Millrace Youth Center
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 38 weeks and will be paid for with $25,000 raised locally.
body: The group has raised $25,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.
Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Millrace library on Monday at 7 p.m. Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Monday mornings.
Ellis Corrigan, who has lived on Fairview Road for 38 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: Letter: Support the After-school Reading Program
body: To the editor: I have lived on Adams Court for 5 years, and I want to say what a difference the Kettle Hill Block Association has made. Please keep the after-school reading program in the budget. Many of us on Adams Court use it every week.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the July meeting.
Joseph Galloway, Bellwood
